column1: Web + Mobile · Phase 1 (deterministic, read-only) → Phase 2 (actions + audit)

column2: A prioritised list of the questions hoteliers actually ask, how ASI Genie handles each one in Phase 1 without touching data, what the user sees, which Roles & Privileges permission gates it, and how the same scenario grows into a Phase 2 action with confirmation and audit.

→ Deterministic answers, summaries, guidance and navigation.
→ Genie NEVER performs an action on the user's behalf.
→ Every answer is filtered by the property's Roles & Privileges matrix (module → feature → READ).
→ Where the user asks for an action, Genie explains and opens the right screen - often with fields pre-filled - so the user completes it in the existing UI.

Genie performs the action through the same PMS APIs the UI uses, after a Preview → Confirm step (hard-confirm for money / irreversible / security; soft-confirm + Undo for reversible). Every write is logged with actor, requested-by, params (PII-redacted) and result, and appears in the Audit Log. Multi-step tasks (night audit, check-in, booking) become guided workflows.

→ Scenarios - the master list (171 scenarios, filterable)
→ Response Types - the card/answer vocabulary
→ Phase 1 vs Phase 2 - the contract between the phases
→ Phase 2 Actions - action catalogue with confirmation tier and audit fields
→ Role Matrix - which typical role can trigger which scenario
→ RBAC Reference - real module/feature names
→ Naming - verbiage alternatives
→ Summary - counts by module, scope and priority.

→ Owner · Admin · Manager · Desk Staff · Housekeeping · Custom .
→ Roles are bundles of permissions; a property can rename or reshape them, so the 'Typical roles' column is a default, not a rule.
→ The server-side 401 Unauthorized / 403 Forbidden on the PMS API is always the final gate.
